This poster was presented at JuliaCon2021.

Abstract:
Simulation is the gold standard for power analysis of mixed-effects models. Traditionally, realistic simulations have been both hard to set up and computationally intractable. Here we present a Julia-based workflow for fast and easy power analysis of mixed-effects models. With MixedModelsSim.jl, we can easily simulate realistic datasets, which we can then quickly analyze with MixedModels.jl. Combined with Pluto.jl, users can explore the impact on power of design decisions interactively.

results.title: A selection correction method for heterogeneous treatment effects in staggered adoption settings - ScienceDirect
results.content: # A selection correction method for heterogeneous treatment effects in staggered adoption settings. With a selection model, heterogeneous treatment effects are identified. This paper proposes an application of Heckman’s (1979) selection correction approach to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects in staggered adoption settings. With a selection model for treatment timing, selection correction terms in counterfactual trends are derived, and the identified counterfactual trends are plugged into the difference-in-differences parameters. Unlike most methods based on interactive fixed effects models, the proposed method does not require a large number of pre-treatment periods. The empirical relevance of the proposed method is illustrated by estimating the short-term effects of first childbirth timing on women’s labor market outcomes. Recently, the estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects has been actively studied in staggered adoption settings. This paper proposes a new application of Heckman’s (1979) selection correction approach to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects. Unlike most methods using interactive fixed effects models, the selection correction method can be applied to setups with a limited number of pre-treatment periods. Recent studies have shown that, in the presence of variation in treatment timing and heterogeneity of treatment effects, the estimation results from two-way fixed effects regressions can provide invalid combinations of average treatment effects (Borusyak et al., 2024, De Chaisemartin and d’Haultfoeuille, 2020, Goodman-Bacon, 2021, Sun and Abraham, 2021). Although the interactive fixed effects models allow non-parallel trends in the counterfactual outcomes, methods based on the interactive fixed effects models generally require a sufficient number of pre-treatment periods. With the parametric models, the treatment effects are identified when parallel trends assumptions are violated due to unobserved confounders and only a limited number of pre-treatment periods is available. This section proposes a selection correction estimator for the heterogeneous treatment effects. This study proposes a new application of Heckman’s (1979) selection correction approach to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects in staggered adoption settings. At the cost of imposing parametric models, the proposed method identifies the treatment effects when non-parallel counterfactual trends include unobserved confounders and a large number of pre-treatment periods is not available. ### Treatment effects in interactive fixed effects models with a small number of time periods.
